skill.name: ship
skill.description: Automates a guarded Git workflow that commits changes, pushes a branch, creates and merges pull requests, and synchronizes branches.
skill.summary: Ship repository changes through an adaptive GitHub Flow or Git-flow release process.
skill.author: cubha

security_audit.summary: The 63 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, a safe fixed Git command substitution, a protective secret-name check, and a text-entropy heuristic. Semantic review found that the skill can publish and merge changes without a final confirmation gate, uses incomplete sensitive-file protection, and does not specify safe shell argument handling.

remediation.issue: Remote commits, pushes, pull request creation, and merges can occur without a final confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Show the planned branch, commit, PR target, and merge method, then require explicit user approval immediately before the first remote write and again before merge.

remediation.issue: The filename-only sensitive-file check is incomplete before git add -A.
remediation.suggestion: Check staged content with a maintained secret scanner, validate ignore rules, and reject known secret formats before committing.

remediation.issue: User-derived messages and branch names are shown in shell-command examples without escaping guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Use argument arrays or vetted Git tool APIs. Validate branch names and pass commit messages as a separate argument, never through shell interpolation.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Remote Merge Without Confirmation Gate
semantic_findings.description: The workflow directs the agent to run the full commit, push, pull request, and merge pipeline after parsing arguments. It does not require a final user confirmation before publishing changes or merging a pull request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly instructs a full pipeline and documents push, PR creation, and merge actions, but no final confirmation checkpoint is described before those external changes.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete Sensitive-File Protection
semantic_findings.description: The sensitive-file check is limited to selected names in git status, followed by git add -A. This can miss secrets in files with other names or existing tracked sensitive files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented filename check is narrow and the subsequent add-all command stages every change. The skill provides no content-based secret scanning or comprehensive ignore validation.

semantic_findings.title: Unspecified Shell Escaping for Commit Messages and Branch Names
semantic_findings.description: The workflow inserts a user-derived commit message and branch placeholders into Git commands without stating quoting or argument-array requirements. An implementation that builds shell strings can allow command injection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source identifies user-supplied arguments and later uses message and branch placeholders in shell-command examples, but it does not prescribe safe command construction.

content.user_title: Ship Changes Through a Guarded Git Workflow
content.value_statement: Release work often requires repeated Git and pull request steps that are easy to perform inconsistently. This skill organizes those steps into an adaptive workflow with verification, review, and branch synchronization guidance.
actual_capabilities: Detects whether the repository uses a develop branch and selects GitHub Flow or Git-flow guidance.
Parses development or main release targets, merge preferences, and a commit message.
Runs a full verification gate when verify.sh is available and reports missing validation.
Requests lightweight security and database schema review before publishing changes.
Creates a feature branch when needed to avoid direct commits to main or master.
Guides pull request creation, merge selection, and branch synchronization after merge.
limitations: It requires a configured Git repository, remote origin, and permission to use GitHub tools.
Verification and review quality depend on scripts and agents available in the repository environment.
The sensitive-file filename check is not a replacement for a content-based secret scanner.
Protected branch rules, CI requirements, and GitHub permissions can prevent completion.

use_cases.title: Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Commit a completed feature, open a pull request to develop or main, and synchronize the branch after merge.

use_cases.title: Release Promotion
use_cases.description: Promote reviewed develop changes to main with a release pull request and a selected merge method.

use_cases.title: Small Team Workflow
use_cases.description: Use a consistent checklist for tests, security review, database review, and pull request creation.

prompt_templates.title: Ship Current Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Ship my current feature branch using the default workflow. Show the planned actions before any remote change.

prompt_templates.title: Merge Into Develop
prompt_templates.prompt: Ship these changes to develop with commit message "feat: add account settings". Run all available checks first.

prompt_templates.title: Promote a Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Ship develop to main using squash merge. Summarize tests, security review, and database review before requesting approval.

prompt_templates.title: Controlled Chain Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Ship my current feature through develop and then main. Stop for confirmation before each pull request merge and report every remote action.

output_examples.input: Ship my current feature branch after checks pass.
output: Planned target: feature branch to develop.
Security review: no critical issues reported.
Awaiting approval before push and pull request creation.

output_examples.input: Promote develop to main with squash merge.
output: Database review: no migration changes detected.
Awaiting approval before creating and merging the release pull request.

best_practices: Review the planned branch, commit message, pull request target, and merge method before approving remote actions.
Keep verify.sh and repository test commands current so the workflow can validate changes reliably.
Use protected branches and required CI checks as independent controls for every merge.
anti_patterns: Do not use the workflow to bypass required reviews, CI checks, or branch protections.
Do not rely on filename checks alone to prevent committing credentials or secrets.
Do not run release actions from a dirty or unrelated branch without reviewing the staged changes.

faq.question: What branching models does this skill support?
faq.answer: It detects a develop branch and guides either feature-to-develop-to-main or feature-to-main workflows.

faq.question: Does the skill run tests?
faq.answer: It runs verify.sh when available and otherwise looks for conventional project validation commands.

faq.question: Can it merge directly into main?
faq.answer: It guides a pull request workflow and is intended to avoid direct commits to protected branches.

faq.question: How does it handle database migrations?
faq.answer: It detects common migration and schema paths, then requests database schema review when available.

faq.question: Does it protect secrets?
faq.answer: It checks selected sensitive filenames, but you should also use a content-based secret scanner and ignore rules.

faq.question: What permissions are required?
faq.answer: You need local Git access, a configured origin remote, and GitHub permissions to create and merge pull requests.
